sanskrit: paraṃ mṛtyo anu parehi panthāṃ yas ta eṣa itaro devayānāt | cakṣuṣmate śṛṇvate te bravīmi- -iha me vīrā bahavo bhavantu ||
english: O Death, go away along that path of yours which is other than the god-trodden way. To those who have eyes and ears I speak: may many heroes be mine here.

sanskrit: ime jīvā vi mṛtair āvavṛtrann abhūd bhadrā devahūtir no adya | prāñco agāma nṛtaye hasāya suvīrāso vidatham ā vadema ||
english: These living ones have turned away from the dead; auspicious has been our invocation of the gods today. We have gone forward to dance and to laugh; endowed with good heroes, may we speak in the assembly.

sanskrit: imaṃ jīvebhyaḥ paridhiṃ dadhāmi maiṣāṃ nu gād aparo artham etam | jyog jīvantaḥ śaradaḥ purūcīs tiro mṛtyuṃ dadhatāṃ parvatena ||
english: I set this barrier for the living; let no other cross over to this purpose of theirs. May they, living long, traverse many autumns, setting Death aside as if by a mountain.

sanskrit: yathāhāny anupūrvaṃ bhavanti yathartava ṛtubhir yanti sākam | yathā na pūrvo aparaṃ jahāty evā tvaṣṭar āyuṃṣi kalpayaiṣām ||
english: Just as the days come in succession, just as the seasons go together with the seasons, just as the earlier does not abandon the later — so, O Tvaṣṭṛ, arrange the life-spans of these.

sanskrit: ā rohatāyur jarasaṃ vṛṇānā anupūrvaṃ yatamānā yati ṣṭha | tān vas tvaṣṭā sujanimā sajoṣāḥ sarvam āyur nayatu jīvanāya ||
english: Mount up in life, choosing old age, striving forward in succession wherever you go. May Tvaṣṭṛ of good birth, in harmony with them, lead all their life-span onward to full living.

sanskrit: aśmanvatī rīyate saṃ rabhadhvaṃ vīrayadhvaṃ pra taratā sakhāyaḥ | atrā jahīta ye asan durevā anamīvān ut taremābhi vājān ||
english: The stony river flows — take hold, be vigorous, cross over, O friends. Leave behind here those who were of ill will; free from disease, may we rise above to the prizes.

sanskrit: ut tiṣṭhatā pra taratā sakhāyo +'śmanvatī syandate nadīyam | atrā jahīta ye asann aśivāḥ śivān syonān ut taremābhi vājān ||
english: Rise up, cross over, O friends — the rocky river rushes here. Leave behind those who were inauspicious; crossing to the auspicious and comfortable, may we rise above to the prizes.

sanskrit: vaiśvadevīṃ sūnṛtām ā rabhadhvaṃ śuddhā bhavantaḥ śucayaḥ pāvakāḥ | atikrāmanto duritāni viśvā śataṃ himāḥ sarvavīrā madema ||
english: Take hold of the gracious speech dedicated to all the gods, becoming pure, bright, and cleansing. Overcoming all adversities, rich in all heroes, may we rejoice for a hundred winters.

sanskrit: udīcīnaiḥ pathibhir vāyum adbhir atikrāmanto 'varān parebhiḥ | triḥ sapta kṛtva ṛṣayaḥ paretā mṛtyuṃ pratyauhan padayopanena ||
english: Going northward by the paths, with winds and waters, surpassing the lower ones by means of the higher — the seers, having gone forth twenty-one times, thrust Death away by the obliteration of footprints.

sanskrit: mṛtyoḥ padaṃ yopayanta eta drāghīya āyuḥ prataraṃ dadhānāḥ | āsīnā mṛtyuṃ nudatā sadhasthe 'tha jīvā vidatham ā vadema ||
english: They who obliterate the footprint of Death, placing an ever-longer life yet further ahead — seated together, push Death away from the common seat; and then, as the living, may we speak in the assembly.

sanskrit: imā nārīr avidhavāḥ supatnīr āñjanena sarpiṣā saṃ viśantu | anaśravo anamīvāḥ suratnā ā rohantu janayo yonim agre ||
english: Let these women, unwidowed and having good husbands, enter the anointing with ghee. Tearless, free from disease, possessed of good jewels, let the women mount the womb-place first.

sanskrit: ime vīrā avidhavāḥ sujānaya āñjanena sarpiṣā saṃ spṛśantām | anaśravo anamīvāḥ suratnāḥ syonād yoner adhi talpaṃ ruheyuḥ ||
english: Let these heroes, unwidowed and of good birth, touch themselves with the anointing ghee. Tearless, free from disease, possessed of good jewels, may they mount from the comfortable womb-place onto the bed.

sanskrit: vyākaromi haviṣāham etau tau brahmaṇā vy ahaṃ kalpayāmi | svadhāṃ pitṛbhyo ajarāṃ kṛṇomi dīrghenāyuṣā sam imāṃ sṛjāmi ||
english: I separate these two with the oblation; with the sacred word I arrange them apart. I make the svadhā-offering undecaying for the Fathers; I release this one together with a long life-span.

sanskrit: yo no agniḥ pitaro hṛtsv antar āviveśāmṛto martyeṣu | mayy ahaṃ taṃ pari gṛhṇāmi devaṃ mā so asmān dvikṣata mā vayaṃ tam ||
english: That Fire of ours, O Fathers, the immortal who has entered into the hearts of mortals — I take that god for myself in my embrace; let him not hate us, and let us not hate him.

sanskrit: apāvartyāgniṃ gārhapatyaṃ kravyādā preta dakṣiṇā | priyaṃ pitṛbhya ātmane brahmaṇe kṛṇuta priyam ||
english: Turn away the gārhapatya fire from the flesh-devouring one; O departed one, go to the south. Make what is dear to the Fathers, to the self, to Brahman — make what is dear.

sanskrit: dvibhāgadhanam ādāya pra kṣināty avartyā | agniḥ putrasya jyeṣṭhasya yaḥ kravyād anirāhitaḥ ||
english: Taking two shares of the wealth, he destroys it through the rite of turning away: that is the Fire of the eldest son who has not been removed from the flesh-devouring function.

sanskrit: yat kṛṣate yad vanute yac ca vastena vindate | sarvaṃ martyasya tan nāsti kravyāc ced anirāhitaḥ ||
english: Whatever he plows, whatever he wins, and whatever he obtains by his garment — all of that belongs to the mortal no longer, if the flesh-devouring fire has not been removed.

sanskrit: ayajñiyo hatavarcā bhavati nainena havir attave | chinatti kṛṣiṃ gāṃ dhanaṃ yaḥ kravyād anuvartate ||
english: He becomes unfit for sacrifice, his luster destroyed; there is no eating of the oblation with him. He cuts off plowing, cattle, and wealth — he who continues to follow the flesh-devouring fire.

sanskrit: bahu gṛdhyaiḥ pra vadaty ārtiṃ martyo ny eti ca | kravyād yam agnir antikād anuvidvān vitāvati ||
english: He speaks much with greedy ones; the mortal enters into distress and comes to ruin — he whom the flesh-devouring fire, closely following him with full knowledge, harasses.

sanskrit: grāhyā gṛhāḥ saṃ sṛjyante yat striyā mriyate patiḥ | brahmaiva vidvān eṣyo yaḥ kravyādaṃ nir ādadhat ||
english: The house becomes fit to be seized, the household is destroyed, when the husband of a woman dies. He alone who is learned in Brahman and who has removed the flesh-devouring fire is the one to be sought out.

sanskrit: yad ripraṃ duritaṃ cakṛmā yac ca duṣkṛtam | āpo mā tasmāc chundhantv agniḥ saṃkasukaś ca yaḥ ||
english: Whatever defilement and transgression we have committed, and whatever evil deed — may the waters cleanse me from that, and the fire called Saṃkasuka.

sanskrit: tā adharād udīcīr āvavṛtran prajānatīḥ pathibhir devayānaiḥ | parvatasya ṛṣabhasyādhi pṛṣṭhe navāś caranti saritaḥ purāṇīḥ ||
english: Those waters, knowing their way, have turned from below toward the north along the god-trodden paths. On the back of the bull-mountain, the ancient rivers run ever fresh.

sanskrit: agne akravyān niṣkravyādaṃ nudā devajanaṃ vaha ||
english: O Agni, you who do not eat flesh — thrust away the flesh-devouring one; carry the company of gods.

sanskrit: imaṃ kravyāt pra viveśa- -ayaṃ kravyādam anv agāt | vyāghrau kṛtvā nānānaṃ taṃ harāmi śivāparam ||
english: The flesh-devouring fire has entered into this one; this one has followed the flesh-devouring fire. Making two tigers face in different directions, I carry away that auspicious other one.

sanskrit: antardhir devānāṃ paridhir manuṣyāṇām agnir gārhapatya ubhayān antarā śritaḥ | jīvānām agne pra tira dīrgham āyuḥ pitṝṇāṃ lokam upa yantu ye mṛtāḥ ||
english: The inner barrier of the gods, the outer boundary of humans — the gārhapatya fire stands between both. O Agni, extend the long life-span of the living; may those who have died go to the world of the Fathers.

sanskrit: sugārhapatyo vitapann arātīr uṣāmuṣāṃ śreyasīṃśreyasīṃ dadhat | sarvān agne sahamānaḥ sapatnān aiṣām ūrjaṃ rayim asmāsu dhehi ||
english: The well-tended gārhapatya fire, scattering enemies, granting each day what is more and more excellent — O Agni, overcoming all rivals, place strength and wealth in these and in us.

sanskrit: imam indraṃ vahniṃ paprim anv ārabhadhvaṃ sa vo nividvān vijahātu mṛtyum | tenāpa hata śarum āpatantaṃ tena rudrasya pari pātāstām ||
english: Take hold of this Indra, the carrier, the fulfiller — he who knows your needs shall drive Death away from you. With him strike away the flying arrow; with him may you be protected all around from Rudra's shaft.

sanskrit: ahorātre anv eṣi bibhrat kṣemyas tiṣṭhan prataraṇaḥ suvīraḥ | anāturāṃ sumanasas talpa bibhraj jyog eva naḥ puruṣagandhir edhi ||
english: You follow day and night, bearing them, dwelling as the guardian, the one who leads across, endowed with good heroes. Bearing the bed of the unailing and cheerful one, be with us a long time, O you who carry the scent of man.

sanskrit: te deveṣv ā vṛścante pāpaṃ jīvanti sarvadā | kravyād yān agnir antikād anuvidvān vitāvati ||
english: They are cut off among the gods and live in evil forever — those whom the flesh-devouring fire harasses from close by with full knowledge.

sanskrit: preva manasā patiti muhur ā vartate punaḥ | kravyād yam agnir antikād aśva ivānuvapate naḍam ||
english: He tumbles forward as if with the mind and turns back again repeatedly — he upon whom the flesh-devouring fire, from close by, scatters itself like a horse scattering a reed.
